summary.title: Transfer Learning: retraining Inception V3 for custom image classification
summary.one_liner: You learn how to adapt a pretrained Inception V3 image classifier to categorize grocery product images by retraining its final layer with TensorFlow's retrain.py script and data augmentation.
keywords: how to retrain a neural network on new classes
takeaways: Transfer learning reuses a pretrained ImageNet model (Inception V3) and retrains only a new top layer, needing less data and time than training from scratch.
Dataset images should be organized into one subfolder per category, and converted to RGB, before training.
Data augmentation (rotation, shifts, shear, zoom, flips) is used to expand a small training set and reduce over-fitting.
The retrain.py script's distortion options make the model more robust to blurry or poorly lit images.
Per the author, roughly 85% accuracy is achievable out of the box, with further gains from fine-tuning hyperparameters.
summary.summary: The author walks through a custom image classification project that categorizes food and grocery product images for a retailer, using TensorFlow v1.1, Python 3.4 and Jupyter. The workflow has three steps: preprocessing (sorting images into category subfolders and augmenting the 3,215 training images with Keras ImageDataGenerator), retraining the bottleneck with Google's retrain.py script on a pretrained Inception V3 model, and testing the saved model on unseen images. The article explains the rationale for transfer learning, the 2048-dimensional bottleneck, and the distortion feature, and links to the author's GitHub code and the TensorFlow image recognition tutorial.
